findings.message: The approach sweep in packages/simulation/src/simulation.test.ts:597-659 ('moors from any approach into the berth's open sides...') skips some of the lanes the task requires it to cover. At line 638, `if (!hullPathIsClear(island, closest.x, closest.y, centre.x, centre.y)) continue;` drops every lane whose closest point to the berth has no clear run to it. That filter is not in the requirement, and nothing is asserted about the dropped lanes. The only guard is a loose floor at line 658: `approaches >= headings.length * 3 * 12`, which lets up to half of the 24 offsets per heading go. The dropped lanes still point into an open side (the headings are 24-56) and their offsets fall inside ±dockRadius, so they are part of the required sweep. The worker's own open assumption says some of these lanes 'run aground there, some outside the reach' (for example head-on at more than ~322 sub-units lateral offset). So the 'never ends up aground outside the reach' clause is untested exactly where the worker says it fails. The filter hides the failure instead of the test catching it. To fix this, either assert the outcome for every lane in the required sweep, or get an acceptance change that narrows the sweep.
findings.requirement: Each case moors on the first step it is inside the reach with a clear path, and never ends up aground outside the reach.

findings.message: No check exercises the new entry script assets/source/maps/sketch.ts or the documented `node assets/source/maps/sketch.ts` command. The root tsconfig.json includes only vitest.config.ts, apps/web/vite.config.ts, tests/** and scripts/**. The drift test in maps.test.ts imports only the pure sliceSeaTmj() from sliceSeaSketch.ts. So sketch.ts is neither typechecked nor run: its `./sliceSeaSketch.ts` import, and whether it writes exactly sliceSeaTmj(), are unverified. No test enforces the split's contract either (no `node:fs` and no side effects at import in sliceSeaSketch.ts). The worker says they ran the command locally, but no verifier check covers it.
findings.requirement: Split the sketch into a pure exported generator (no `node:fs`, no side effects at import) and a small entry script that writes the file, keeping the documented regeneration command working.
